title: Normal Operation Indicator
shortDescription: The fridge is running normally — N is a status indicator, not a fault.
fullDescription:
On Norcold N-series fridges the letter N on the diagnostics display simply indicates normal operation with no stored faults. It can be mistaken for an error by new owners.

If the fridge is not cooling despite showing N, the fault is mechanical (cooling unit) rather than electronic. Norcold boards only flag electrical faults.

Check physical cooling performance if you suspect a problem.

fixSteps.title: Confirm cooling
fixSteps.instruction: Use a fridge thermometer to verify temperature is in range.

whenToCallPro: Only if cooling is insufficient despite normal status — indicates cooling unit failure.
videoSearchQuery: Norcold RV fridge N display meaning

title: Ammonia Recirculation / Cooling Unit Error
shortDescription: The fridge detected abnormally slow cooling and flagged a cooling unit fault.
fullDescription:
ArEr on Norcold N-series indicates the control logic sensed that the boiler temperature rose but the cold box didn't get cold enough in the expected time. This typically means the ammonia solution isn't recirculating — a failing cooling unit.

Common causes include off-level storage, overheating, or age-related sediment in the boiler tube. ArEr is often terminal for the cooling unit.

Norcold N6/N8 cooling units were subject to a major recall for fire hazard — verify your unit isn't on the recall list before continued use.

causes.cause: Sediment in boiler tube from age or off-level use

symptoms: Burner runs but fins stay warm

fixSteps.title: Attempt boil-tube tap
fixSteps.instruction: With unit cold, gently tap boiler tube to dislodge sediment — short-term fix only.

fixSteps.title: Verify level
fixSteps.instruction: Park dead level and retry cooldown.

fixSteps.title: Schedule cooling unit replacement
fixSteps.instruction: If fault persists, full cooling unit replacement is required.

whenToCallPro: Any persistent ArEr — cooling unit replacement requires specialized training.

faq.a: Power-cycling may clear the display but if the unit is truly failed, the error returns within hours.

title: General System Fault / Board Reset Needed
shortDescription: The control board has detected a non-specific fault and requires reset.
fullDescription:
Error 99 is a catch-all Norcold code — it means the board lost track of state or encountered a logic fault. Often caused by voltage spikes, brief power loss, or EEPROM corruption.

First-line fix is a 5-minute power-off of both AC and DC. If the code returns, board replacement is usually the next step.

Disconnect shore power, generator, and house battery — all three energize the board.

fixSteps.title: Full power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect shore power, generator, and house battery for 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Verify voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Reconnect and confirm 12V DC is stable at the fridge.

fixSteps.title: Replace eyebrow board
fixSteps.instruction: If 99 returns, replace the display/eyebrow board.

whenToCallPro: If multiple power cycles don't clear 99 and board replacement is outside your comfort zone.

faq.a: It may work short-term, but repeated errors indicate a real board problem.

title: Boiler Tube Thermal Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The boiler tube high-temperature safety sensor has tripped or is out of range.
fullDescription:
The boil tube sensor (often called a thermal fuse or high-temp switch) sits against the boiler and opens the heating circuit if temperature exceeds safe limits. Norcold issued a recall adding this sensor to prevent cooling unit fires.

A tripped boil sensor means either the cooling unit overheated (dangerous) or the sensor itself failed. Many owners simply replace the sensor, but this defeats the safety and should not be done if there's any sign of leak.

Yellow residue on the boiler or an ammonia odor means the cooling unit has ruptured — stop using immediately.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for leak
fixSteps.instruction: Check behind fridge for yellow/green stains or ammonia smell — if present, STOP.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermal sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Only if no leak — install new Norcold thermal sensor kit.

whenToCallPro: If any leak, residue, or smell present — fire hazard.

faq.q: Should I just bypass the thermal sensor?
faq.a: No — it's a mandatory safety feature following the Norcold recall.

title: No 120V Input Detected
shortDescription: The fridge is not receiving 120V AC power for the heating element.
fullDescription:
When switched to AC or Auto mode, Norcold fridges expect 120V at the power board. NO AC indicates the voltage sensing circuit sees less than ~90V.

Check the dedicated 15A breaker, the GFCI outlet (sometimes daisy-chained), and the inline plug behind the fridge.

Do not bypass GFCI — it protects the fridge outlet from wet-bay moisture.

causes.cause: Tripped GFCI in bath or galley
Failed AC sensing on power board

symptoms: Works on shore but not generator or vice versa

fixSteps.title: Reset breakers and GFCIs
fixSteps.instruction: Check all GFCI outlets in the RV and reset the fridge breaker.

fixSteps.title: Reseat AC plug
fixSteps.instruction: Access rear via exterior vent and reseat plug.

whenToCallPro: If 120V confirmed at plug but fridge still reports NO AC — power board fault.

faq.q: Can the fridge still run on gas?

title: Propane Ignition Failure
shortDescription: Fridge attempted gas ignition but failed to sense flame.
fullDescription:
NO GAS on Norcold N-series means the module sparked, opened the gas valve, and did not detect flame rectification within the trial window. After 3 attempts the unit locks out.

Common: spider webs in burner tube (80% of post-storage cases), low propane, dirty orifice, or degraded electrode.

Close propane tank before removing the burner for cleaning.

fixSteps.title: Test propane
fixSteps.instruction: Light stove to confirm propane supply.

fixSteps.title: Clean burner
fixSteps.instruction: Remove burner, blow out with compressed air.

fixSteps.title: Inspect electrode
fixSteps.instruction: Check for cracks and correct spark gap (~1/8 inch).

whenToCallPro: If you smell gas or the solenoid valve is suspect.

faq.a: Mud daubers nest in warm flues; cover vents during storage.

title: Low 12V Supply Voltage
shortDescription: The house battery voltage has fallen below the fridge minimum.
fullDescription:
Norcold boards need at least 10.5V DC to operate the gas valve and control logic. Below that, LO DC appears and the unit shuts down to prevent erratic behavior.

Common on boondocking trips where the house battery isn't recharged. Also triggered by loose battery terminals or a failed converter.

Recharge or connect to shore power before continuing.

fixSteps.title: Measure battery
fixSteps.instruction: Check voltage at house battery terminals.

fixSteps.title: Charge battery
fixSteps.instruction: Connect shore or run generator for 1 hour minimum.

whenToCallPro: If voltage is good at battery but LO DC persists — wiring resistance issue.
videoSearchQuery: Norcold LO DC low voltage fix

faq.q: Can I just increase the cutoff?
faq.a: No — the 10.5V limit protects the solenoid valve from misfire.

title: Generic Fault Flag
shortDescription: A fault is stored; check diagnostic display for specific code.
fullDescription:
The letter F on the main eyebrow display means a stored fault exists. Press and hold the DIAG button (or the combo per model) to view the detailed code (e.g., ArEr, 99, boil).

Without pulling the diagnostic, F alone isn't actionable. Always read the stored code before attempting repair.

causes.cause: Any subsidiary fault stored in memory

fixSteps.title: Retrieve diagnostic code
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the MODE button while powered on to display the underlying code.

whenToCallPro: Depends on the underlying code retrieved.

faq.a: Fix the underlying fault first — F clears when the specific error resolves.

title: Door Ajar Warning
shortDescription: The fridge door has been open too long or the reed switch failed.
fullDescription:
Newer Norcold 2118 and 1210IM models include a door alarm. DOOR or d-oP indicates the reed switch has reported an open door for longer than 4 minutes.

First check that the door is actually closed and the magnetic seal is intact. If the warning persists with the door closed, the reed switch (near the hinge) may be stuck.

causes.cause: Door actually open or seal damaged

fixSteps.title: Close door firmly
fixSteps.instruction: Verify positive latch and no bottle blocking seal.

fixSteps.title: Test magnet alignment
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm magnet on door lines up with switch in frame.

fixSteps.title: Replace reed switch
fixSteps.instruction: Remove trim and swap switch if stuck.

whenToCallPro: If door seal or hinge damage requires door alignment.

faq.q: Can I disable the door alarm?
faq.a: Some models allow muting via the DIAG menu, but it returns on next power cycle.

title: Cold Check / Cooling Unit Monitor Fault
shortDescription: The cold-check logic has not seen expected freezer temperature drop.
fullDescription:
On Norcold 1210/1200 series, CO indicates the cooling check firmware saw insufficient temperature drop at the freezer after a set runtime. Similar root cause to ArEr but less severe.

Check thermistor placement first, then ambient conditions (hot desert camping with solar on the side wall can overload the absorption cycle).

causes.cause: High ambient / direct sun on fridge side

fixSteps.title: Reposition thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm bead is on correct fin per owner's manual.

fixSteps.title: Shade the vent
fixSteps.instruction: Install a reflective cover on the exterior vent in high ambient.

fixSteps.title: Add vent fan
fixSteps.instruction: Install 12V vent fan to improve airflow behind fridge.

whenToCallPro: If CO persists after thermistor and ventilation fixes — cooling unit is degrading.

faq.q: Does a vent fan really help?
faq.a: Yes — chimney airflow behind the fridge can improve capacity 10-20%.
